title: Ferrite-Dichalcogenide Nanocomposites for Energy Storage Applications
content: Hybrid nanocomposites have emerged as promising materials to address the increasing demand for efficient, high-performance energy storage systems. Ferrite-dichalcogenide nanocomposites have garnered significant attention due to their unique physicochemical properties. This paper focuses on synthesizing, characterizing, and applying nano zinc ferrites (ZnFe2O4) and a few-layered molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) nanocomposite for energy storage applications. The ZnFe2O4 NS were prepared via a hydrothermal approach, which involved dissolving Zn(CH3COO)2 and FeCl3 in ethylene glycol and varying molar concentrations of CH3COONa as a surfactant. The resulting homogeneous mixture was transferred into a stainless-steel autoclave and heated at 180 °C for 24 hours. Afterward, the product was collected via centrifugation, thoroughly washed with distilled water, and vacuum-dried at 65 °C for 24 hours. The synthesis of few-layered MoS2 samples was accomplished by dispersing a nominal amount of commercial MoS2 material in acetone and deionized water. Subsequently, the dispersion underwent ultrasonic treatment in iced water for 1 hour with ultrasonic power set at 550 watts. Following the ultrasonic treatment, the resulting black dispersion was centrifugated, and the supernatant liquid was subsequently collected by drying the solution in a vacuum at 65 °C for 24 hours. The MoS2/ZnFe2O4 nanocomposites (NCs) were synthesized using the hydrothermal method. Different molar amounts of a few-layered MoS2 were mixed with Zn (CH3COO)2, FeCl3, and CH3COONa and subsequently dissolved in C2H6O2 to have NCs with various molar ratios.
